tob-10234: The Diamond Sutra is one of Buddhism’s most treasured texts: a dialogue in which the Buddha teaches that everything we see is like a dream, a bubble, a flash of lightning — empty of any lasting self. This insight lies at the heart of Mahayana Buddhism. William Gemmell’s translation presents the compact sutra; its 868 CE printed copy at Dunhuang is the oldest dated printed book known.
tob-9334: The Didache — the Teaching of the Twelve — is the oldest church handbook to survive, a first-century rule for washing, fasting, prayer, and the holy meal. Found in a Constantinople house of monks in 1873 by Bryennios, it startled the learned with its peep at earliest Christian wont. Short text; huge weight.
tob-4185-78134: The first volume of Goodwin’s five-book Plutarch opens the Moralia — pieces on rearing, on hearkening, on sifting flatterers from friends. These are antiquity’s kindliest self-betterment writings. The edition brought Plutarch the moralist to English readers.
tob-4134: Isaac Myer’s Qabbalah was America’s first weighty book on the Kabbalah — its teachings, story, and book-lore, drawn straight from Hebrew wells. Out in 1888, it opened Jewish holy-mystery to English readers. Scholars still cite Myer’s trail-work. It stays a honored first guide to the field.
tob-10034: Mackail’s Englishing of Virgil’s Field-Book gives the great tilling-poem — four books on tilth, trees, kine, and bees. Maecenas bade him write it, to heal Rome’s war-torn farms. The poem is the crown of Latin teaching-verse. This printing bears his praise of field-life to English readers.
cia-0000112334: A June 1990 summary of the Soviet TASS news agency's press review for July 22. TASS digests told Western analysts what Moscow wanted its public — and the world — to be reading. The document is media monitoring as statecraft: understanding the Soviet Union through the news it chose to amplify.
cia-0000119734: A September 1956 overview titled simply The Hungarian Situation. Before the October explosion, Hungary was already the bloc's trouble spot — the file was thickening. The document is the baseline against which the coming revolution would be measured.
cia-0000124334: A June 1958 retrospective on the Soviet earth satellites of 1957 — Sputnik's first year, assessed with some distance. The shock had faded; the analysis had deepened. The document looks back at the year the sky changed, with cooler eyes.

The finding touched the raw nerve of America's nuclear presence in Japan. The document shows an ally questioning the atomic umbrella.

a-popular-history-of-ireland-from-the-ea: This edition of Thomas D'Arcy McGee's beloved history brings Ireland's story — from misty origins to the winning of Catholic Emancipation — to a new generation of readers. McGee writes as both scholar and patriot, making centuries of struggle vivid and personal. An enduring, heartfelt telling of the Irish past.
arxiv-2605-08734: Fine-tuning giant models on a budget usually means LoRA, which trains small low-rank patches instead of updating every weight. Ziyun Liu, Fengmiao Bian, and Jian-Feng Cai sharpen the idea with AdaPreLoRA, preconditioning those patches with the Adafactor optimizer for faster, steadier learning. The 2026 paper is optimization research for practitioners adapting large models cheaply.
arxiv-2605-08834: On February 27, 2023, a brilliant fireball streaked over northern Sweden — and cameras built to watch the aurora caught it. Gabriel Borderes-Motta, Daniel Kastinen, Tima Sergienko, and colleagues analyze those auroral-imaging observations to reconstruct the meteor's path and behavior. The paper turns a sky-watching accident into planetary science.
arxiv-2605-08934: Mechanistic interpretability reverse-engineers neural networks neuron by neuron; compositional interpretability asks how those pieces combine into larger meanings. Ward Gauderis, Thomas Dooms, Steven T. Homer, and Kola Ayonrinde chart the path from one to the other. The 2026 paper is a perspective piece on where interpretability research should go next.
arxiv-2605-09034: Zeroth-order optimization tunes models using only function values — no gradients — and spectral methods organize the search. Jiahe Chen and Ziye Ma accelerate it with partial orthogonalization drawn from power iteration. The 2026 paper is optimization for the gradient-free world.
arxiv-2605-09134: Programs that fix their own bugs get better when the repair agent learns from actually running the code. Yuanhao Li, Hongbo Wang, Xiaotang Shang, and colleagues boost automated program repair with execution-grounded reinforcement learning guided by dual reward models — BoostAPR. The 2026 paper trains fixers on real executions, not just static code.
arxiv-2605-09334: Mahler's conjecture — about the minimum volume of a convex body and its polar — is a crown jewel of convex geometry; the non-symmetric case in three dimensions is the frontier. Shibing Chen, Yuanyuan Li, Dongmeng Xi, and Zhe-Feng Xu tackle it. The 2026 paper is convex geometry on a famous open problem.
arxiv-2605-09534: Security operations centers increasingly lean on AI, and someone must govern the partnership. Elyson A. De La Cruz, Rishikesh Sahay, and Md Rasel Al Mamun offer a design science framework for operational decision support. The 2026 paper is governance for the AI-augmented SOC.
arxiv-2605-09734: Language models learning to use tools continually need supervision over whole trajectories, not just final answers. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy B, Sagnik Chatterjee, and colleagues provide trajectory supervision for continual tool-use learning. The 2026 paper teaches tool use that keeps improving with practice.
arxiv-2605-09834: Bayesian inference is only as good as its priors, and AI can inform those priors — if done reliably. Jongwoo Choi and Sean O'Hagan supercharge Bayesian inference with reliable AI-informed priors. The 2026 paper is Bayesian statistics with machine-learned judgment.
arxiv-2605-09934: Multimodal tool-using agents act through tools across modalities — and their outputs need verifiable provenance, proof of origin. Bihui Yu, Caijun Jia, Jing Chi, and colleagues build TRACER: verifiable generative provenance. The 2026 paper is AI accountability for agentic tool use. It makes every tool call traceable.
plos-pone-0003434: Veterinary virologists found where foot-and-mouth virus hides in this 2008 paper. The highly contagious livestock virus persists in the light zone of germinal centers, the training grounds inside lymph nodes where immune cells learn. Locating this refuge helps explain why the virus lingers and complicates eradication of a disease that cripples animal trade.
plos-pone-0003534: Cancer biologists caught the esophagus changing identity in this 2008 paper. In Barrett's esophagus, the normal flat lining transforms into a glandular type, a premalignant switch, and the team showed two genes, Cdx1 and c-Myc, drive that transdifferentiation. Naming the initiators points to where intervention might halt the march toward cancer.
plos-pone-0003634: Transplant immunologists Widmann, Sester, and Gärtner tracked the virus-watchers after stem-cell transplants in this 2008 paper. Levels of CMV-specific CD4 T cells rose and fell in step with cytomegalovirus replication in patients. The tight correlation makes these T cells a living gauge of the most common viral threat transplant recipients face.
plos-pone-0003734: In 2008, Maeda, Inose, and Matsuo found wandering cells keeping their shape in step. With no signal to follow, moving cells still coordinated their deformation with their motion in ordered patterns. The study reveals an inner choreography behind the seemingly aimless crawl of cells.
plos-pone-0003834: Working in 2008, a team tested whether extra womb fluid shortens the cervix in twin pregnancies. Their controlled study in complicated polyhydramnios cases measured cervical length against amniotic fluid volume. The results clarify when excess fluid truly threatens preterm birth.
plos-pone-0003934: In 2008, Vieira, Arzabe, and Hernandez measured a Brazilian toad population. They recorded body-shape variation in Proceratophrys cristiceps across its range. The morphometric survey captures how one toad species varies in form. The baseline data anchor future studies of this South American amphibian.
plos-pone-0004034: In 2008, Xue, Sun, and Zhang discovered new gene regulators in a worm parasite. They identified and characterized novel microRNAs from the blood fluke Schistosoma japonicum. The parasite causes schistosomiasis, a major public-health burden across China. The new microRNA catalog opens fresh targets against the worm's complex life cycle.
plos-pone-0004134: In 2009, Kakiuchi, Ishigaki, and Oslowski traced a mood drug's ripple effect. Valproate, a mood stabilizer, boosted WFS1 expression and tuned its ER-stress protein partners. The bipolar drug's molecular trail clearly widened. The WFS1 link hints at new mood-drug targets ahead.
plos-pone-0004234: In 2009, Liang, Zhang, and Wang found immune guards in lancelet eggs. Alternative complement activity in amphioxus egg cytosol fought microbes. Outside fertilized eggs face germ-filled waters. The ancient defense predates modern immunity. The finding pushes immune origins deeper in animal history.
plos-pone-0004334: In 2009, a team found two distinct nerve endings. Varicone and growth-cone tips proved two kinds of nerve endings. The two tips behaved quite differently. The neat split clarifies nerve-growth models. The work sharpens a classic cell model of nerve outgrowth.
plos-pone-0358534: Parkinson’s disease steals balance and movement — and exercise is one of the few defenses. The PARKEX study compared basic training against dual-task programs, where patients move while thinking, on physical function in Parkinson’s. The head-to-head results guide therapists choosing the most effective workout.
plos-pone-0345434: Some children get ear infection after ear infection. This study mined electronic health records for early-life factors predicting recurrent acute otitis media. The predictors it found let pediatricians spot high-risk infants early and intervene before the cycle takes hold.
plos-pone-0351534: Why did some countries’ students ace PISA 2022 science while others stumbled? This paper found recurrent, system-specific model-attribution patterns across nine education systems. The patterns show how each system’s features explain its science performance — a diagnostic for education ministers.
plos-pone-0357034: Maize pests eat profits across millions of small farms. WSD-YOLO is a lightweight YOLO-based model with enhanced feature representation for maize pest detection. The efficient model is designed to run on modest devices, bringing AI-powered pest scouting directly to the cornfield.
plos-pone-0357834: Banana bunchy top disease devastates harvests — and newly planted gardens get re-infected with cruel speed. This paper identified the drivers of banana re-infection in fresh plantings within endemic zones. The findings give growers a practical recovery playbook for bringing banana production back from the brink.
plos-pone-0358034: Shiplifts hoist entire vessels over dams — and capsizing during the lift is the nightmare scenario. This paper built surrogate modeling based on computational fluid dynamics to predict the capsizing moment in a coupled shiplift system. The fast surrogate keeps these engineering marvels operating within safe limits.
plos-pone-0355734: Solving systems of nonlinear equations demands iterative schemes that converge fast. This paper proposed a hybrid accelerated iterative scheme based on the Picard–Ishikawa approach. The accelerated mathematics reaches solutions quicker than its predecessors, speeding up countless engineering computations.
plos-pone-0354634: Tea plant necrotic ring blotch virus threatens tea harvests — and Iran’s isolates were unmapped until now. This paper reported the first complete genome sequences of the virus from Iranian tea plants, plus transcript expression profiling. The genomic foundation enables diagnostics and resistant breeding for a vital crop.
plos-pone-0354334: Mesothelin — a cell-surface protein — may be pancreatic cancer’s Achilles’ heel. This pan-cancer profiling study unveiled the diagnostic potential and therapeutic targetability of MSLN in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The findings nominate mesothelin-directed therapies for one of oncology’s deadliest diseases.
plos-pone-0356234: Carbapenemase-producing gut bacteria — resistant to last-resort antibiotics — are spreading in Ethiopian hospitals. This Addis Ababa cross-sectional study measured multidrug resistance and carbapenemase production in clinical Enterobacteriaceae isolates. The surveillance data are a warning flare for antibiotic stewardship.
plos-pone-0354234: Human resilience might be engineered one person at a time. DELTA is a protocol for strengthening human biological resilience with an N=1 digital health and dynamic biomarker approach. The personalized protocol treats each individual as their own experiment — the vanguard of truly precision health.
plos-pone-0355934: Electrical grounding systems can be improved with biodegradable waste — turning trash into safety. This paper measured and analyzed grounding enhancement using biodegradable waste soil additives. The findings offer a sustainable route to better electrical safety in regions where conventional materials are scarce.
plos-pone-0354134: Spotted wing drosophila — Drosophila suzukii — ravages fruit crops on schedules growers need to know. This automated long-term field monitoring revealed its diel and seasonal activity patterns. The around-the-clock data tell farmers exactly when the pest strikes — so sprays hit their mark.
plos-pone-0354734: Radiation exposure might be readable from a simple skin swab. This paper explored monitoring exposure through skin swab multi-omic profiling. The non-invasive approach could transform how we assess radiation doses — from nuclear workers to radiotherapy patients to accident victims.
europmc-pmc2914634: Killing malaria for good means knowing its ecology first. This 2010 paper argues field ecology must come before elimination and eradication drives. The authors show mosquito and parasite habits shape whether campaigns succeed. Their call grounded big eradication dreams in ground truth rather than wishful thinking.
europmc-pmc2924334: Doctors dragged their feet on digital records, and this 2010 paper asks why. The authors first pool the studies, then sort the roadblocks into groups, then match each group with fixes. Their map guides clinics past doctor pushback. The work sped the move from paper charts to screens.
europmc-pmc2926634: Valproic acid steadies seizures and moods, but its full story runs deeper. This 2010 review covers what the old drug can do at the molecular level, where it helps, and where it harms. The authors weigh new tricks against known risks. Their overview guides safer, smarter use.
europmc-pmc2996334: A heart-risk RNA comes in straight and looped forms. This 2010 paper shows expression of linear and circular forms of an INK4/ARF non-coding RNA tracks atherosclerosis risk. The authors reveal the correlation. Their work points to heart markers.
europmc-pmc3022534: Mouse embryos got a gene activity atlas. This 2011 paper maps gene activity across the growing mouse embryo in fine detail. The authors' atlas reveals development unfolding. Their resource aids embryo research. Every organ's debut gets its close-up. The atlas is free for all to browse.
europmc-pmc3047434: Telomere length got a precise measure. This 2011 paper brings a PCR test that reads absolute telomere length. The authors' method steadied aging studies. Their tool spread through labs. Short telomeres flag cellular old age. Stress researchers adopted it at once.
europmc-pmc3102034: Study differences got measured. This 2011 paper shows how Q statistics quantify disagreement across trials. The authors' guidance steadies reviewers. Their work shaped methods. Wild disagreement warns against pooling. The paper gives worked examples. Reviewers now report Q routinely. Cochrane adopted the approach.
europmc-pmc6532434: MicroRNAs are tiny RNA snippets that tune which genes stay active, and a few engineered RNA drugs have already reached patients. This review surveys the next wave: microRNA-based medicines moving through preclinical and clinical research. It covers how these molecules could serve as both disease biomarkers and therapies - and the delivery hurdles still standing in the way.
europmc-pmc6587234: Cells crawl, invade, and stick - behaviors behind wound healing, immune defense, and cancer spread. This hands-on guide covers the lab assays that measure all three: imaging migrating cells and crunching the numbers. With protocols from setup to data analysis, it gives researchers a complete toolkit for studying cell movement.
europmc-pmc6602434: Bacteria and fungi hide drug blueprints in their DNA - clusters of genes that brew antibiotics and other potent chemicals. antiSMASH 5.0 is the upgraded genome-mining pipeline that finds these clusters automatically. The tool accelerates the hunt for new natural products in an era of dwindling antibiotics.
europmc-pmc6614034: Ischemic heart disease still tops global death charts - but the picture shifts by country and decade. Analyzing WHO mortality data from 2005 onward, researchers charted who dies of it, where, and how trends moved. The country-level patterns separate real progress from statistical illusion.
europmc-pmc6616534: Ginger is more than a spice - its rhizome packs phenolic compounds, terpenes, and other bioactives. This review catalogs ginger's chemical constituents and the health effects tied to them: anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and more. The authors sort strong evidence from folk claims for one of the world's favorite roots.
europmc-pmc6688334: piRNAs - tiny RNA strands that partner with PIWI proteins - were thought to guard only sperm DNA. This review reveals their second act in cancer: misbehaving piRNA/PIWI complexes that drive or suppress tumors. The emerging players may yield new biomarkers and drug targets.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-34: GAO's 2007 report looks at a bold fix for clumsy agencies: put a top boss in charge of just running the shop. The chief operating officer idea splits policy from plumbing, giving one leader the job of making the agency work. The report tracks how agencies tried the role — and whether the new bosses truly changed how business got done.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1034: The world's anti-slavery projects were flying half-blind in 2007 — GAO's report says U.S.-backed trafficking programs lacked solid tracking, though experts saw fixes. The findings pair a measurement gap with a reform sketch. Good intentions, the report argues, need good yardsticks to free anyone.
gao-gaoreports-b-309734: Florida and Vermont's Medicaid experiments drew GAO's legal eye in 2007 — were the waiver approvals properly done under the law? The ruling tests the demonstration projects against the statute's fine print. Health-policy labs, the call reminds, still need a solid legal foundation to stand on.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-734: Ultrasound billing needed a second opinion in 2007 — GAO's report weighs payment reforms and tech-qualification rules for the scans. The findings probe whether Medicare paid right for the pictures. The report's question is dollars and sense: fair price, qualified hands.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-634: Airport screening rules were finally getting risk-based in 2007 — GAO's report says threat levels, hard experience, and passenger gripes drove the changes. The findings grade the new approach. The report's balance: safer skies without treating every grandma like a suspect.
openalex-w7206159834: The city of Bayeux in Paraiba got its name from the French town freed by the Allies in World War II. This study reconstructs the city's political history and identity through the pages of the Paraiba newspaper A Uniao in 1944. The author shows how wartime news shaped local memory. A fine piece of press-based history, reading a city's story in the ink of its time.
openalex-w7204657734: A cat arrived at the clinic with a suspicious lump, and tests pointed to fibrosarcoma, a tumor of connective tissue. This case report walks through how the vets diagnosed it and chose treatment, noting that the tumor's location did not match the usual vaccine-linked pattern. The authors share the case to help other vets recognize similar ones. Short, clinical, and useful at the exam table.
openalex-w7204540334: Trajan was Rome's first emperor born outside Italy, in the province of Hispania. This history article studies how that province's ties with Rome set the stage for his rise at the end of the first century AD. The authors trace the politics of integration and power that made a provincial the most powerful man in the world. Ancient history with a modern echo about outsiders reaching the top.
openalex-w4414920434: PrSb2 hides a weird electric signal inside its magnetic state. This lab paper reports voltage tests revealing a twist-based Hall effect, a sign of knotted magnetic patterns, in its ordered phase. The team tied it to the crystal's charge waves. A study of math-like twists showing up in a real crystal.
openalex-w4413733734: A crystal's defects can flip its thermoelectric sign. A materials-theory study of disorder as a design knob.
openalex-w4412648834: Light can be guided along protected paths that ignore defects. An optics review of light that refuses to scatter.
openalex-w7129071434: Surgeons sometimes nick the gallbladder during keyhole removal, but does it matter to patients? This study tracked pain and daily life after such accidental tears. The team filled a gap in what we know. A surgery study of a common slip and its aftermath.
openalex-w7165044234: College students need someone to talk to. This study tracked use of counseling rooms at two Juntendo University campuses, which serve over 3,000 students. The team mapped who sought help and why. A campus mind-health study of demand meeting supply.
pmc-13471634: A 2026 environmental health study linking components of fine-particle air pollution (PM2.5) to reduced blood flow in the brain. The authors trace a pathway through inflammation — markers in the blood that suggest the body's immune response is the middleman. The finding adds weight to evidence that dirty air harms the brain, not just the lungs.
pmc-13511134: This 2026 software paper presents the ESL-PSC Toolkit, a visual tool for linking shared genetic changes to convergent phenotypes — traits that evolved independently in different species. pmc-13453334: This 2026 aging study put older adults through a supervised exercise program and found it restored physical activity levels while improving multi-omic biomarkers of frailty — molecular signatures measured across genes, proteins, and metabolites. pmc-13420334: A 2026 diagnostics paper showing that single-cell gene expression analysis of monocytes can distinguish Kawasaki disease — a childhood vasculitis — from viral infection with high specificity. pmc-13488434: A 2026 chemistry paper on organic photoredox-catalyzed TEMPO disproportionation — a mild platform for in situ oxoammonium ion formation. The light-driven method was gentle. The platform serves synthesis.

pmc-13473334: In this 2026 study, the association between physical activity and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis was examined — improper sitting posture as a mediator. The posture mediated the link. The association is the finding.
pmc-13472934: In this 2026 retrospective PET/CT study, metabolic tumor volume and total lesion glycolysis predicted prognosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The imaging metrics forecasted survival. The predicting aids hematology.
pmc-13399234: A 2026 reply letter to a prospective observational study on ventriculitis incidence and outcomes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients. The correspondence engages the findings. The reply is the scholarly exchange.
pmc-13475834: A 2026 therapeutic challenge: a 5-year-old girl with Gorlin-Goltz syndrome and cardiac fibroma. The rare syndrome's heart tumor was managed. The challenge is the case.
pmc-13448034: In this 2026 spine surgery paper, the question was posed: decompression alone or with extended fusion for adjacent-segment pathology after lumbar fusion? The surgical dilemma was examined. The paper weighs the options.
pmc-13426234: A 2026 prospective controlled study asking whether extracorporeal shock wave therapy is more effective in younger patients for mild-to-moderate erectile dysfunction (the title is truncated). The age-treatment interaction was tested. The asking is the clinical question.
pmc-13461534: A 2026 multicenter RCT protocol for warm acupuncture's efficacy and safety in oxaliplatin-induced chronic peripheral neuropathy. The protocol is the plan. The trial will test the traditional therapy.
pmc-13418534: This 2026 biomaterials paper showed dynamic stiffness enabled stage-specific properties mediating functional endothelialization on vascular implants. The smart stiffness guided the endothelium. The enabling is the implant design advance.
arxiv-2606-15934: An astronomy paper studying WASP-189b, one of the hottest known exoplanets. On ultra-hot Jupiters, a "cold trap" keeps heavy atoms out of the upper atmosphere — until extreme heat breaks it down, letting metals like titanium appear in the air. The authors analyze telescope observations to explain how and when this shift happens on the scorched world.
arxiv-2606-16034: AI tools that sort events over time — like spotting the flash when a fault starts — often sound surer than they are. This paper fixes that at run time: it tunes the tool's trust scores as it works so they match the truth. It is for AI folk who build time-based sorters.
arxiv-2606-16134: Syllogistic logic — the "all men are mortal" kind of reasoning — has been studied since Aristotle, and its computational complexity since the 1990s. This paper revisits the average-case complexity of multilevel syllogistic, starting from a 1995 Courant technical report and carrying the results into a Lean 4 formalization — machine-checked proofs of the old claims.
arxiv-2606-16334: Vision-language models can describe images, but do they understand time — before and after, cause and effect? ChronoSuite is a benchmark exposing their "chronological blindness," testing temporal reasoning in models that see and read. The paper gives AI researchers a way to measure and fix this gap in video understanding.
arxiv-2606-16434: Cells fade, and duff cells can strand rides or grids. This paper stands up lone, soup-to-nuts cell-health guessers that read a cell's life prints from its hum over time. For pack crews who must flag tired cells first. Early flags save fires and funds.
arxiv-2606-16534: Labs now let bot scribes ink their big-iron code — here in Julia, the tongue of number labs. This paper grades the ink: is it true, side-by-side swift, and big-proof? A frank report card for big-iron crews who weigh bot scribes.
